title: Integral proper base change on localizing categories
statement:
For a cartesian square with $p:X\to Y$ proper, $g:Y'\to Y$, $p':X'\to Y'$ and
$g':X'\to X$, the base change map $g^*Rp_*\to Rp'_*g'^*$ is an isomorphism of
functors $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))\to\Loc(\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text:
On $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ the base change map is an isomorphism: this is the
completed proper base change (the case $f=p$ proper of
[thm-cbc-complete-proetale]), where completed and uncompleted pullback agree
on integral constructible complexes. Both $g^*Rp_*$ and $Rp'_*g'^*$ are exact
and preserve direct sums on the localizing categories: $g^*$, $g'^*$ always
do, and $Rp_*$, $Rp'_*$ do by [sk-prop-int-compactness]. The objects on which
the natural transformation is an isomorphism thus form a localizing
subcategory containing $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, hence all of
$\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ ([sk-lem-sf-determination]). This is the
argument of [sk-prop-proper-base-change-unbounded] with the integral
estimates of [sk-prop-int-compactness].
